system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Overall read:** The Seller package is not "fair and balanced." It collapses every protection into one 20%/18-month general regime (including title, fraud, indemnities and pre-Completion liabilities), relies on blanket data-room disclosure plus a "discoverable" knowledge bar, and pushes three hard-money items (Riverlark ~$3.2m, bonuses $420k, Ironquay $180k) and one unresolved revenue condition (Bluefen ~30% of revenue) past Completion. Note also the disclosure cut-off is 22 September 2026 — six weeks stale as at today; the letter must be brought down to signing and Completion.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for all Warranty Claims.
- Buyer wants: Cap of 100% of price for Fundamental/Title/Tax; general warranty cap at 30–50% (≥ AUD 7.2m–12m); indemnities and specific DD items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006) uncapped or separately capped at price.
- Recommendation: Reject 20% as a universal cap; counter at ≥35% for general warranties with fundamental/tax/indemnities at price.
- Reason: A single 20% cap underprices known, quantified risks that already exceed AUD 4m in aggregate exposure.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only recovery.
- Buyer wants: De minimis ≤ AUD 10,000 (with related claims aggregated); basket ≤ AUD 120,000 (0.5%); tipping ("first dollar") basket; thresholds not applying to Title, Tax, Fundamental, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: Counter at AUD 10k / AUD 120k, tipping basket, aggregation of related claims, carve-outs as above.
- Reason: At AUD 25k the de minimis alone would exclude most individual DD-008/DD-011 (AUD 110k each) type items once split or disclosed piecemeal, and an excess-only basket is below-market for a AUD 24m deal.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months after Completion for notification; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated."
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (two audit cycles); Tax – 7 years / 4 years after relevant assessment period; Title/Fundamental – 7 years or no limit; delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- Recommendation: Counter at 24 months general, statutory-aligned for tax, 7 years fundamental; strike the catch-all.
- Reason: 18 months captures only one post-Completion audit and the catch-all silently imports the general time bar into every other regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- Buyer wants: Separate regime — cap at 100% of price (minimum), 7-year (or unlimited) limitation, no de minimis/basket, no disclosure qualification.
- Recommendation: Reject outright; non-negotiable.
- Reason: "Administrative simplicity" would mean the Buyer could recover only AUD 4.8m if it turns out it did not get the shares it paid AUD 24m for.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature" — no fraud carve-out stated.
- Buyer wants: Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default of the Seller or its officers/advisers.
- Recommendation: Insert full carve-out; also carve out specific indemnities, leakage and Completion covenants.
- Reason: A clause purporting to limit liability for fraud is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability — its presence signals the whole limitation package is over-reaching.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"; nothing in the letter admits anything (para 1.4).
- Buyer wants: Disclosure only of matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; data room disclosed only via an indexed, agreed USB copy; no disclosure of public records (or limited to ASIC company extract and PPSR on a named date); specific disclosures listed against specific warranties; Disclosure Letter brought down at Completion with no new disclosures permitted to qualify Completion-date warranties.
- Recommendation: Reject blanket disclosure; impose "fair disclosure" standard, index, and reject public-register disclosure.
- Reason: Combined with cl 8.3, blanket data-room/public-record disclosure would extinguish warranty protection for almost every known issue.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge of, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- Buyer wants: Delete. At most: actual knowledge of a named short list of deal-team individuals, and only where the matter was fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter — never constructive or "discoverable" knowledge, never advisers' knowledge.
- Recommendation: Delete; fall back to actual knowledge of named individuals only, with no "discoverable" limb.
- Reason: "Discoverable" imposes constructive knowledge of everything in a data room and all public registers — it is effectively a complete waiver of warranty claims.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: Reasonable endeavours; condition "treated as satisfied" on delivery of written consent; Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: A true Condition Precedent to Completion — unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, in form approved by Buyer; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; no "deemed satisfaction"; waivable by Buyer only; if not obtained, Buyer termination right or price reduction/retention. Warranty that Bluefen has not threatened termination.
- Recommendation: Hard CP with Buyer-approved form of consent; no deeming language.
- Reason: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of revenue; a consent that is "satisfied on delivery" of a conditional or non-compliant letter leaves 30% of the business at risk on day one.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: Release "to be provided following Completion"; DL confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge included.
- Buyer wants: Consistent with debt-free/cash-free — repayment and release at or before Completion: executed payout letter from Riverlark, deed of release and discharge of all security, PPSR discharges, delivered at Completion; facility repaid from Seller proceeds via funds flow (price adjustment); Seller indemnity for any residual bank liability; address cl 8.1 change-of-control event.
- Recommendation: Completion deliverable, funded from the purchase price in the funds flow; reject post-Completion release.
- Reason: A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with AUD 3.2m secured debt and a change-of-control default — the opposite of "debt-free."

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow; DL silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: Bonuses, superannuation, payroll tax and all on-costs (est. AUD 480–500k gross) treated as Transaction Costs/Debt in the price mechanics — deducted from price or funded by the Seller through the funds flow and paid through Company payroll at Completion; specific indemnity for any shortfall; warranty that no other Completion-triggered payments exist.
- Recommendation: Itemise in funds flow as a price deduction (grossed up for on-costs) with a specific indemnity.
- Reason: "A matter for the Seller" means nothing when the obligor is the Company — the Buyer would be paying them from day one.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment of AUD 180k; "considered adequate."
- Buyer wants: Pre-Completion deliverable — proof of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment/IP deed from Ironquay under cl 7.3; failing that, a retention of ≥ AUD 180k plus an uncapped specific indemnity covering non-transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, infringement claims, re-development costs and loss of use; indemnity outside caps, thresholds and time limits.
- Recommendation: Require payment and confirmatory assignment at Completion; expand the indemnity to cover ownership/use loss, not just the fee.
- Reason: The exposure is not AUD 180k but loss of title to the deliverables — cl 7.3 withholds ownership until every fee is cleared.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: DD-006 is "preliminary operational," not material; DL confirms ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address, scope/access/notification unresolved, no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: Completed investigation before signing (or at least before Completion) with report delivered to Buyer; Seller to make any OAIC/affected-individual notification decision under the Privacy Act in consultation with Buyer; specific indemnity (outside caps/baskets/time limits) for regulatory penalties, notification costs, claims, remediation and reasonable legal costs; privacy and data-handling warranties unqualified by this disclosure; escrow if unresolved at Completion.
- Recommendation: Specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation deliverable; reject "not material" characterisation.
- Reason: An uncontrolled export of 1,240 personal records is a potential notifiable data breach with civil-penalty exposure that dwarfs the basket and sits squarely in the warranty period.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: Three renewals (AUD 110k each, AUD 330k aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs"; DL does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: Clarify timing and whether committed pre-Completion; if committed/accrued for pre-Completion periods, include in Working Capital/Debt adjustment; if post-Completion discretionary, confirm terminability; prohibit Seller entering or renewing them between signing and Completion without Buyer consent (interim covenants); note the related renewals must be aggregated so they cannot each fall under the AUD 25k/110k thresholds.
- Recommendation: Treat as price-mechanic/working-capital item and require aggregation; do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence.
- Reason: Three related AUD 110k commitments split across documents look structured to sit under thresholds and outside locked-box/leakage protection.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated; one regime for warranties, title, indemnities, non-reliance.
- Buyer wants: Discrete liability regimes: (1) general warranties; (2) Fundamental/Title/Capacity; (3) Tax warranties and Tax indemnity; (4) specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006, Bluefen); (5) Completion covenants, leakage and price-adjustment claims; (6) fraud — each with its own cap, threshold and time limit, and with the general regime never applying by default.
- Recommendation: Redraft Clause 12 as a schedule of categories; strike the "unless expressly stated" default.
- Reason: Category collapse is the mechanism by which every other Seller concession is undone — fix this and SPA-N-001 to 005 largely follow.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: Title evidenced solely by the Company share register at DD-012; DL expressly notes it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."
- Buyer wants: Independent verification before signing — current ASIC company extract and members' register, PPSR search (any security over shares), review of constitution/shareholder agreement for pre-emptive rights, historical transfer/allotment documents and share certificates; Seller delivers share certificates, signed transfers, director resolutions and register update at Completion; unqualified title warranties under the Fundamental regime.
- Recommendation: Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and make Completion deliverables explicit; do not rely on the register alone.
- Reason: The Seller has deliberately flagged that the register is the only source and that the Buyer has not verified it — that is an invitation to carry the risk.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket, data-room disclosure).
- Buyer wants: Tax — full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, cap at price, limitation tied to ATO amendment periods (4 years from assessment, longer for fraud/evasion), no basket; IP — unqualified warranties of ownership, no infringement, employee/contractor assignment, open-source compliance; Ironquay-specific position per SPA-N-011; IP warranty cap at price or ≥50%, 3-year limitation; neither qualified by general data-room disclosure.
- Recommendation: Treat as open, not settled; table a separate tax deed/indemnity and IP warranty schedule.
- Reason: The Company is an analytics business — IP is the asset being bought, and 18 months is shorter than any tax amendment period.

---

**Priority for the mark-up:** (1) SPA-N-014/004/005 structural fixes; (2) SPA-N-009 and SPA-N-010 funds-flow corrections (hard cash ~AUD 3.7m); (3) SPA-N-008 Bluefen CP; (4) SPA-N-006/007 disclosure and knowledge; (5) SPA-N-011/012 specific indemnities; (6) economics in SPA-N-001/002/003. Also require the Disclosure Letter to be re-dated and brought down to signing — the current 22 September cut-off is already stale.
=== END ADVICE ===
